chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: Andy Kirk's telegram: joining in St. Louis
summary: Andy Kirk wires him; he meets the band in St. Louis, starts at seventeen dollars a night and gets raises through manager Billy Shaw.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: telegram from Andy Kirk, telling me to join him...
Well, how did he know about you?
I think the manager from Hamp's band had told him that I was a good trumpet player. Because I know nobody else wouldn't have known about me out East.
Where was Kirk at the time?
He was in New York. That's where I got the wire from. So he told me to meet...

Yeah. He told me to meet the band in St. Louis. And I said, "Oh yeah? Okay" -- at the Tune Town Ballroom. So I went on out there and met him. He was a beautiful cat when I first... The first time I met him, he was really beautiful. He said, "Well, how are you?" I said, "Oh, I'm fine, sir. I'm fine. Yeah, how you doin'?" So he talked to me. He said, "Well, I don't have no uniforms, so you'll just have to wear a tuxedo." And I said, "Well, that's all right. I've got one." But then again, I said, "How much do I get?" So he said, "The best I can do right now is seventeen dollars a night." I said, "Okay, that's all right. I can go for that." So I told Billy Shaw two weeks later, I said, "I asked Andy for a raise, and he told me to see you, said it's all right with him." So he did. He raised me up to nineteen dollars. I
said, "Now, this sounds more like what I was interested in." And the longer I stayed there, every time I'd go to Billy for a raise, I would get it!
Billy Shaw. He was our manager, yeah.
I think you told me you were writing for that band, too.
You weren't with Hamp long enough to write for him.

No, I had my own music playing with Hamp, so when I got ready to leave, I just took it up. I just sort of passed it in. Every time we'd play a number that I wrote, I would pass that in. So I took my music with me and I put it in Kirk's band, and it sounded good like a motherfucker. We swung the shit out of it.
